title: introduce-pricebook-driven-batch-shaper-and-quant-compat-mapper
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Customers want deterministic unit economics decisions surfaced at deploy time. Existing heuristics focused on prefills and ad-hoc batch presets; this PR introduces a pricebook-driven approach that ties SKU/hardware pricing and model-specific quantization compatibility data to batch-shaping defaults and fallback policies.

What this PR does: Adds a pricebook schema and generator, a Batch Shaper service that ingests pricebook entries and workload signals to emit tenant-scoped batch-shape defaults, and a Quant Compatibility Mapper that analyzes model artifacts and produces safe-quant fallthroughs (e.g., int8-fp16 fallback chains) for the serving runtime. Includes a CLI dry-run tool for offline simulation of cost/latency tradeoffs.

Design notes: The pricebook is a small YAML manifest (examples/pricebook/*.yaml) describing unit GPU-hour prices by region/SKU, plus per-quant-profile compute multipliers and storage cost estimates. The Batch Shaper evaluates per-tenant request size distributions and outputs recommended batch shapes and target batch windows in the defaults catalog. The Quant Compatibility Mapper runs lightweight artifact checks (codec signatures, tensor dtype footprints) and produces a compatibility map used by the runtime router to select compatible quantized variants when primary variants are unavailable. Fallback policies are conservative by default and annotated with a reason and confidence score so rollouts can be gated.

Implementation summary: - pricebook/schema.yaml: schema + validator and generator (tools/pricebook/gen_pricebook.py) - service/batch_shaper/: batching policy engine, deterministic rule evaluator, unit-econ estimator - tools/quant_mapper/: artifact scanner, compatibility heuristics, lockfile writer used by runtime - cli/pricebook_sim.py: offline sim that produces delta cost/latency estimates per tenant - telemetry: new metrics prefixed with econ.pricebook.* and runtime.quant_compat.*

Testing and rollout: Added unit tests for generator/validator and end-to-end integration tests that run the offline simulator against small workload traces. CI had a flaky integration test initially (timeout on macOS runner) which was re-run and resolved; overall CI green. Rollout plan: staged canary to 5% of tenants, monitor econ.pricebook.recommendation_delta and runtime.quant_compat.fallback_rate, then 25%, then full release. Feature gated behind feature flag econ.pricebook.enabled.

Docs and migration notes: docs/pricebook.md documents the YAML format and examples. Operators can provide a custom pricebook via the console or place a pricebook.yaml in /etc/redwood/pricebook/ for Private installs. Backwards compatibility: if no pricebook is present the Batch Shaper falls back to current default heuristics.

Related: ENG-1453 (pricebook design), PM-378 (product requirements).
